lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice A: the addition rule

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt: P(A and B) = 3/20, P(B) = 5/20. Find P(A|B).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 6/20, P(B) = 6/20, and P(A and B) = 1/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.

items.prompt: A box holds 12 items, of which 6 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 2/20 and P(B) = 10/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 6/20, P(B) = 7/20, and P(A and B) = 4/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A box holds 6 items, of which 4 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 54/100 and P(B) = 64/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Given P(A) = 4/20, P(B) = 5/20, and P(A and B) = 1/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, the probability of a delay is the same whether or not it is raining. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: Delay and rain are independent, because conditioning on rain does not change the probability of a delay.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
